# Publishing setup

One-time steps to wire up petstore's release pipeline (release-please, then
goreleaser publishing a GitHub Release and a Homebrew cask).
If you're using Claude Code, `.claude/skills/setup-publishing/SKILL.md` walks
through the same steps interactively; this is the checklist by hand.

## 0. Put the repo on GitHub

Skip if this repo already has a GitHub remote.

- [ ] ```sh
      git init -b main && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: initial generated repo"
      gh repo create oxmonty/petstore-cli --source=. --push
      ```

## 1. Let release-please open PRs

release-please proposes releases from a workflow-created pull request; GitHub
blocks this by default on new orgs and repos.

- [ ] At `https://github.com/oxmonty/petstore-cli/settings/actions` (or the
      org-level equivalent), under **Workflow permissions**, check "Allow
      GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests".
- If this is skipped, the release-please run fails with "GitHub Actions is
  not permitted to create or approve pull requests."

## 2. Homebrew tap

- [ ] Create the `oxmonty/homebrew-tap` repo. It must be **public** — a
      private tap breaks installs.
- [ ] Create a fine-grained PAT at
      `https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new`: resource
      owner `oxmonty`, repository access limited to `homebrew-tap` only,
      permission **Contents: read and write**, nothing else.
- [ ] Store it as the `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` secret, e.g.
      `gh secret set HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN --org oxmonty --visibility all`.
      On a free org plan, org secrets only reach public repos.

## 3. npm (only if you distribute via npm)

This repo does not ship an npm publish pipeline yet — biscuit templates one
in a later release. These steps apply once you add npm distribution.

- [ ] Enable 2FA on the publishing npm account — publishes fail with a hard
      403 without it.
- [ ] A brand-new npm package can't use OIDC trusted publishing on its first
      publish. Bootstrap it once locally:
      ```sh
      npm login
      npm publish   # or your publish script, once one exists
      ```
- [ ] Then configure a trusted publisher for each package at
      `https://www.npmjs.com/package/<name>/settings`: publisher "GitHub
      Actions", this repo, the release workflow's filename, "Allow npm
      publish" only. Needs npm >= 11.5.1 / Node >= 22.14.
- [ ] npm points a package's `latest` dist-tag at its very first publish, even
      a prerelease. Promoting a later prerelease is manual:
      `npm dist-tag add <package>@<version> latest`.

## 4. Graduating from prerelease to stable

Not a one-time step — do this when the first stable release is ready.
release-please never graduates on its own; with prerelease versioning it
increments the prerelease counter forever (alpha.4, alpha.5, ...).

- [ ] Remove `"prerelease": true` (and any `"prerelease-type"`) from
      `release-please-config.json` and commit. The next release PR proposes
      the stable version — everything downstream (the GitHub release flag,
      the stable cask) keys off the version string automatically.
